## OVERVIEW
This policy is developed to regulate and structure all leave types within the organization, ensuring fair, transparent, and timely management of leave requests, with clear guidelines for different leave entitlements.
## SCOPE
This policy applies to all permanent employees of the company.
## ELIGIBILITY
Paid leaves are applicable to all employees after confirmation. An employee who is on probation can avail Paid leaves only under special circumstances.
Maternity leaves are applicable for employees who have worked for at least 80 days during the 12 months immediately preceding the date of her expected date of delivery of child in that particular establishment according to the Maternity Leave Act, 1961. Maternity leave will be available to female employee for a maximum of 26 weeks
## POLICY
## Qualitative Objectives:
- Ensure fair and timely allocation of leave based on employees' needs and business requirements.
- Promote a healthy work-life balance by providing adequate leave to employees while ensuring business continuity.
- Maintain transparency in the leave process, enabling employees to manage their time-off efficiently.
## Quantitative Objectives:
- Ensure that 100% of employee leaves (paid, unpaid, sick, maternity, etc.) are accurately recorded in the leave management system within 48 hours of application/approval.
- Maintain 0 reported cases of leave misuse, unauthorized absenteeism, or policy violation per year.
Leave year is from 1st Jan. to 31st Dec. Employees who are appointed during the year shall be entitled to leaves on pro-rata basis.
## Leave type & entitlement:
[table]
| Type | Entitlement |
| Casual Leave | 07 working days |
| Sick Leave | 07 working days |
| Paid Leave | 21 calendar days |
| Maternity Leave | 26 weeks |
| Paternity Leave and Child Adoption Leave for Male employees | 05 working days |
| Exemption Leave | Upto 60 working days |
| Child Adoption Leave for Female employee | 180 days |
| Saturday Off (Executives only) | 1 Saturday off per month |
## PROCEDURE
## Casual Leave:
This leave is intended to meet to personal requirements of an employee but not for the vacations. They are emergent and incidental in nature.
## Rules and regulations:
- A maximum of seven (07) days of leave will be permissible per annum.
- Only a maximum of (03) consecutive days of Casual leave will be allowed in a month if taken without being clubbed with any other leaves.
- Casual leave taken between Gazettes holidays/weekly off will be considered.
- If Casual leave exceeds more than 03 consecutive days, then thereafter leaves will be considered or marked as Paid leaves.
## This leave can neither be accumulated & carried forward nor encashed.
## Sick leave:
Sick leaves are allowed on account of an employee's temporary inability to perform duties because of sickness or injury.
## Rules and regulations:
- A maximum of seven (07) days leave will be permissible per annum.
- The employee availing sick leave should take appropriate measures to inform the HOD or Reporting Manager and HR regarding the probable duration of her/his absence immediately on commencement of leave.
- The employee should submit a Leave Application Form duly approved by the HOD or Reporting Manager to the HR department within three (3) days after resumption of duty otherwise it will be treated as Paid leave.
- If leaves exceed two days then, the employee should submit a Leave Application Form duly approved by the HOD or Reporting Manager along with Medical Certificate by a registered Medical Practitioner to the HR department within three (3) days after the resumption of duty otherwise it will be treated as Paid leave.
## This leave can neither be accumulated, carried forward nor encashed.
Exemption leave.
Exemption leave is provided to those employees who have met with a critical accident or have serious illness.
## Rules and Regulations:
- An employee is entitled to avail of this leave if he/she has met with an accident or is going thru a serious illness provided the employee/or a close relative of the employee has submitted supporting medical documents.
- This leave can be availed for a maximum for 60 days.
- Exemption leaves will be availed at the rate of basic salary of the respective employees up to 60 days.
## This leave can neither be accumulated, carried forward nor encashed.
Paid leave.
Paid leave is a privilege that the company provides to its employees to spend quality time with their families, relax and unwind or for any purpose that requires time away from office each year.
## Rules and regulations:
- An employee is entitled to avail of twenty-one (21) calendar days’ Paid leaves per annum.
- Applications for Paid leaves, duly approved by HOD or Reporting Manager/Department Head, should be submitted at least fifteen (15) days in advance to the HR department. Paid leaves should preferably be taken at the less busy time of the year, if possible.

## OVERVIEW
Efficient Plastech Private Limited is committed to maintaining a productive, fair, and supportive work environment by ensuring responsible management of working hours, providing fair compensation, and offering flexible work options to support work-life balance
## SCOPE
This policy applies to all employees of Efficient Plastech Private Limited, including permanent, contractual, full-time, and part-time staff across all locations and departments.
## POLICY
## QUALITATIVE OBJECTIVES
- Promote employee well-being by maintaining fair and transparent working hour practices.
- Provide equitable compensation and benefits, reflecting extra efforts like overtime.
- Foster a work culture that values flexibility and recognizes diverse employee needs.
- Ensure timely and confidential grievance resolution related to working conditions.
## QUANTITATIVE OBJECTIVES
- Maintain 100% compliance with local and national labor laws.
- Ensure 100% of employees are informed about compensation policies during induction.
- Ensure all overtime records are maintained and reviewed monthly.
- Maintain employee grievance resolution turnaround time within 15 working day
## WORKING HOURS & OVERTIME MONITORING
- Working hours are structured in compliance with the Factories Act and applicable labor laws.
- Supervisors and HR regularly review attendance and time records to detect overtime or irregular working patterns.
- Rest breaks (15 minutes) are given after every 3.5 hours of work, and a 30-minute lunch break is provided (flexible timing).
Efficient Plastech promotes flexible working practices such as:
- Flexi-time: Allowing flexible start and end times within a predefined bandwidth.
- Job Sharing: Employees may mutually agree to share roles based on part-time needs.
- Work-from-home: Granted on a case-by-case basis where work permits remote delivery.
- Part-time opportunities: Available based on department workload and role compatibility.
These arrangements are provided to support personal needs and encourage work-life balance, subject to operational feasibility and manager approval.
## GRIEVANCE MECHANISM ON WORKING CONDITIONS
- A formal grievance mechanism exists for employees to report concerns related to working hours, wages, overtime, or work conditions.
- Employees can raise complaints anonymously via email, Suggestion box, or in-person discussion with HR.
- All grievances are addressed confidentially with strict non-retaliation protection.
- HR ensures resolution within 15 working days and maintains records for audit purposes.
- Flexi-time, work-from-home (where operationally feasible), and job-sharing arrangements are available to support employees' personal circumstances and reduce stress related to work-life imbalance
- Part-time opportunities are considered based on department requirements and employee needs
- Pregnant employees are provided with modified duties, reduced hours, or lighter tasks as required
## A.4 Awareness & Education
- Awareness sessions on stress recognition, mental health, and coping strategies are conducted at least twice a year for all employees and workers
- Sessions are delivered in the local language where necessary to ensure accessibility
- Mental health awareness content is displayed on notice boards at all facilities
- New employees receive information on mental health support channels as part of their induction training
A.5 Open Communication Channels The following channels are available to all employees to raise concerns, seek guidance, or simply be heard:
[table]
| Channel | Details | Availability |
| Direct conversation with HR | In-person, confidential discussion | Working hours |
| Grievance Email | grievance@efficientengg.com | 24 x 7 |
| Suggestion / Grievance Box | At all facilities | Always accessible |
| Anonymous reporting | Via suggestion box or anonymous email | 24 x 7 |
| Direct conversation with Manager | Informal, supportive discussion | Working hours |
| GRC Member | Grievance Redressal Committee member | Working hours |
All disclosures related to mental health or stress are treated with strict confidentiality and full non-retaliation protection.
## A.6 Anti-Harassment & Anti-Discrimination
- The company's Internal Complaints Policy (ICC), Anti-Discrimination Policy, and Disciplinary Policy actively work to eliminate bullying, harassment, and discrimination — which are among the leading causes of workplace psychological harm
- Zero tolerance is maintained for any behavior that creates a hostile, intimidating, or demeaning work environment
- Refer to Section EH 02 for full details of these policies
## A.7 Employee Recognition & Engagement
- Employee contributions are acknowledged through performance appraisals, internal recognition, and career development opportunities
- Internal talent mobility and promotion policies provide employees with a sense of growth, purpose, and progression — all of which are known protective factors against workplace stress

chapters.title: Grievance Redressal Policy
chapters.text:
## OVERVIEW:
Efficient Plastech Private Limited is committed to maintaining an environment of fairness, respect, and transparency. This policy ensures that employees—both permanent and contractual—have the right to voice concerns about any perceived unfair treatment, providing a mechanism for resolving conflicts in a timely and effective manner.
## SCOPE:
This policy applies to all permanent and contractual employees of Efficient Plastech Private Limited, covering all types of grievances related to unfair treatment, employment-related decisions, or any action that negatively impacts their employment.
## POLICY:
## Qualitative Objectives:
- Ensure Equal Opportunity for All Employees: Guarantee all employees, regardless of position or seniority, have equal access to grievance redressal mechanisms.
- Fairness and Transparency: Maintain an open, transparent, and non-biased approach throughout the grievance resolution process.
- Employee Engagement: Foster a supportive environment where employees feel comfortable voicing concerns without fear of retaliation.
- Timeliness of Resolution: Ensure that grievances are resolved at the earliest possible stage, reducing prolonged dissatisfaction.
## Quantitative Objectives:
- Grievance Resolution Time: Resolve 80% of grievances at the first informal stage within 7 days.
- Escalation and Final Decision: Ensure that 95% of unresolved grievances are escalated and resolved at higher levels within 30 days of formal submission.
- Employee Satisfaction with Grievance Process: Achieve at least 90% employee satisfaction with the grievance resolution process, as measured by post-resolution surveys.
## GOVERNANCE AND RESPONSIBILITY:
## Grievance Redressal Committee (GRC):
- Composition: The GRC will consist of 6 members: 3 workmen and 3 staff members, with a minimum of 3 women members to ensure diverse representation.
- Chairperson: The HR Manager will act as the Chairperson of the Committee, ensuring impartiality and compliance.
- Responsibilities: The committee will review grievances, recommend resolutions, monitor the grievance process, and ensure the timely implementation of solutions.
## Management Responsibility:
- The Compliance Officer will oversee the overall implementation and governance of this policy and ensure compliance with the objectives and procedures.
- Line Managers will be responsible for resolving informal grievances and facilitating the escalation of unresolved issues.
## Greivance reporting Procedure:
- The Grievance Committee shall be held once every Six months.
- Employees should attempt to resolve grievances informally by addressing them directly with their immediate supervisor or manager within 5 days.
- Managers must make efforts to resolve grievances promptly, ensuring objectivity and discretion.
## Formal Grievance Submission:
- If the grievance is not resolved informally, the employee must submit a written grievance to the HR Department, detailing the issue, previous attempts at resolution, and any supporting evidence (including dates, locations, and context).
## Grievance Committee Review:
- The Grievance Redressal Committee will meet within 15 days to review formal grievances and propose resolutions. If necessary, the committee will escalate the issue to senior management.
## Escalation Process:
- If the grievance remains unresolved after the committee’s consideration, it will be referred to the most senior manager for final resolution. A written decision will be provided to the employee within 30 days.
## ACCESS TO GRIEVANCE CHANNELS:
- Grievances can be reported directly to the HR and Compliance Departments. The Management Committee will be informed of the grievance status, ensuring no conflict of interest in resolving issues.
## MEANS OF REPORTING GRIEVANCES:
- Suggestion Box: Employees may submit grievances anonymously.
- Written Letters or Emails: Employees can submit formal grievances through a letter or email to grievance@efficientengg.com.
- Direct Interaction with Committee Members: Employees can approach members of the Grievance Redressal Committee during scheduled sessions.
- Whistleblower Channel: Employees can also use the whistleblower mechanism to report grievances confidentially to ensure their concerns are addressed impartially.
## MONITORING AND REVIEW MECHANISM:
- Annual Grievance Audit: The effectiveness of the grievance handling process will be audited annually, reviewing the number of grievances raised, their resolution rates, and employee satisfaction levels.
- Quarterly Reports: The HR Department will submit quarterly reports to senior management on grievance statistics, escalation patterns, and outcomes.
- Continuous Improvement: Feedback from employees and management will be collected to continually improve the grievance redressal system, ensuring that it meets both qualitative and quantitative objectives.

chapters.title: Anti-Discrimination and Equal Opportunity Policy
chapters.text:
## OVERVIEW
Efficient Plastech Private Limited is committed to fostering an inclusive, respectful, and equitable work environment. In alignment with Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) 5 – Gender Equality and SDG 10 – Reduced Inequalities, we strive to ensure that all employees are provided with equal employment opportunities and are free from discrimination and harassment of any kind.
## SCOPE
This policy applies to all permanent and contractual employees of Efficient Plastech Private Limited, as well as any third-party contractors, vendors, or service providers involved with the company.
## POLICY
It is the policy and firm commitment of Efficient Plastech Private Limited to provide a work environment that is free from any form of discrimination or harassment. The company will not tolerate discrimination based on race, age, color, gender, sexual orientation (including LGBTQ+), language, remuneration, employment grade, national origin, migration status, physical or mental disability, religion, or any other personal characteristic. We are dedicated to ensuring that all individuals are treated with respect and dignity, promoting equality and fairness in all aspects of employment.
## Qualitative Objectives:
- Promote Equal Opportunity and Fair Treatment: Ensure that all employees have equal access to employment, development, and advancement opportunities based on merit, not discrimination.
- Foster a Respectful Work Environment: Create a culture of mutual respect where every employee feels valued, included, and empowered to contribute.
- Encourage Inclusivity: Promote diversity in all aspects of employment, including gender, race, nationality, disability, and other forms of diversity.
- Prevent Harassment and Intimidation: Eliminate any behavior that creates a hostile work environment, ensuring everyone feels safe and respected.
## Quantitative Objectives:
- Zero Tolerance for Discrimination and Harassment: Aim for 100% of reported incidents of discrimination or harassment to be addressed within 30 days of the complaint.
- Employee Training Completion Rate: Ensure that 95% of employees undergo annual training on discrimination, harassment prevention, and inclusivity.
- Employee Satisfaction with Work Environment: Achieve 90% or higher satisfaction ratings in employee surveys regarding fairness, inclusivity, and respect in the workplace.
## GOVERNANCE AND RESPONSIBILITY:
## Management Responsibility:
- The AVP - Strategy & Procurement is responsible for overseeing the implementation of this policy and ensuring that it is consistently enforced across all levels of the organization.
- The HR Department will ensure that all employees are educated about this policy and provide necessary support in case of grievances.
- Managers and Supervisors are expected to lead by example and actively promote an inclusive and respectful work environment.
## Policy Enforcement:
- The Compliance Officer will regularly monitor the effectiveness of this policy and take necessary actions to ensure compliance.
- The Management Committee will review any serious violations and ensure appropriate corrective actions are taken.
## Discrimination Reporting Procedure & Remediation Procedure: Investigation and Corrective Action
## Complaint Process:
Employees who believe they have experienced or witnessed discrimination or harassment should report the issue promptly, either in writing or verbally, to their immediate supervisor, HR Department, or any member of the Management Committee.
## Escalation Process:
Upon receiving a complaint, HR will review the issue and escalate it to management for a full investigation. Both parties involved in the complaint will be given an opportunity to present their perspectives.
## nvestigation and Action:
If the complaint is substantiated, appropriate corrective actions will be taken. Depending on the severity of the issue, this could range from counseling or training to termination of employment.

## EQUAL OPPORTUNITIES & WORKPLACE INCLUSION POLICY
## OVERVIEW
Efficient Plastech Private Limited believes that a truly inclusive workplace — where every individual feels valued, respected, and empowered to contribute fully — is not just a moral obligation but a strategic advantage. Diversity of background, experience, perspective, and identity makes our organization stronger, more innovative, and more resilient.
This policy goes beyond prohibiting discrimination. It establishes active, operational programs and initiatives designed to promote equal opportunities, build an inclusive culture, and ensure that every employee — regardless of gender, age, caste, religion, disability, sexual orientation, nationality, or socio-economic background — has a genuine and equal chance to succeed at Efficient Plastech Private Limited.
This policy is aligned with Sustainable Development Goal 5 (Gender Equality), SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth), SDG 10 (Reduced Inequalities), and the Ethical Trading Initiative (ETI) Base Code.
## SCOPE
This policy applies to:
- All permanent and contractual employees across all locations (Mumbai Office, Virar Factory, Haridwar Factory)
- Trainees, apprentices, and part-time workers
- All stages of the employment lifecycle — recruitment, onboarding, training, development, promotion, and separation
- Third-party contractors and vendors working on company premises
## POLICY STATEMENT
Efficient Plastech Private Limited commits to:
- Actively promoting equal opportunities at every stage of the employment lifecycle
- Creating and sustaining an inclusive work environment where all employees feel a genuine sense of belonging
- Implementing structured programs and initiatives — not just policies — to drive real inclusion outcomes
- Tracking diversity and inclusion metrics and using data to identify and address gaps
- Holding managers and leaders accountable for inclusive behaviors and outcomes within their teams
- Continuously improving inclusion practices based on employee feedback and evolving best practices
## UNDERSTANDING INCLUSION
Efficient Plastech Private Limited recognizes that equal opportunity requires active effort — not just the absence of discrimination. The company is committed to addressing the following barriers to inclusion that commonly exist in workplaces:
- Unconscious bias in hiring, promotion, and performance evaluation decisions
- Structural barriers that prevent certain groups from accessing opportunities
- Cultural or language barriers that exclude minority or migrant workers
- Physical barriers that limit participation of differently abled employees
- Lack of visible role models from underrepresented groups in senior positions
- Informal networks and relationships that advantage some employees over others
## OPERATIONAL PROGRAMS & INITIATIVES

## Purpose:
Efficient Plastech Private Limited is committed to fostering a professional, open, and trusting workplace, free from sexual harassment, mental harassment, and abusive language. It is our policy to ensure all employees are treated with respect and dignity, and that all forms of harassment are promptly addressed, ensuring a safe, respectful work environment for everyone.
## SCOPE
This policy applies to all permanent, contractual, temporary, part-time employees, trainees, consultants, and any third-party workers engaged with Efficient Plastech. It includes all incidents of sexual, mental, and verbal abuse, both within and outside of working hours, including work-related functions, conferences, business trips, and client interactions.
## POLICY STATEMENT
Efficient Plastech does not tolerate sexual harassment, mental harassment, or abusive language. These behaviors include, but are not limited to:
- Sexual Harassment: Unwanted sexual behavior, including physical contact, requests for sexual favors, and the display of offensive materials.
- Mental Harassment: Verbal abuse, bullying, or behavior that causes distress, anxiety, and emotional harm.
- Abusive Language: The use of foul, threatening, or belittling language intended to demean others.
We recognize that such behaviors undermine individual dignity and impact mental well-being, which can affect the overall work environment. All complaints of harassment are taken seriously and will be investigated promptly and confidentially.
## Qualitative Objectives:
## Promote a Safe and Respectful Work Environment:
- Foster a work culture where all employees, regardless of gender, race, or background, feel safe and respected.
- Ensure that all employees are aware of the consequences of sexual harassment, mental harassment, and abusive language through training and communications.
## Timely Reporting and Action:
- Ensure all employees feel comfortable reporting incidents of harassment, with assurance of a confidential and respectful process.
- Provide support to employees reporting harassment by offering counseling and other resources as needed.
- Deliver comprehensive training to all employees, emphasizing the importance of recognizing and addressing harassment in the workplace.
- Establish mentorship programs where senior employees lead by example and promote a harassment-free environment.
## Employee Well-being:
- Offer support mechanisms such as counseling for those who have experienced harassment or verbal abuse.
- Ensure that harassment does not negatively impact an employee's mental health or career progression.

chapters.title: Whistle Blowing Policy
chapters.text:
## OVERVIEW
The Whistle Blower Policy aims to eliminate malpractices within the company by encouraging employees and business associates to report concerns regarding unethical behaviors, mismanagement, misuse of company assets, financial fraud, and other forms of wrongful conduct. This policy ensures that whistle- blowers can disclose such concerns without fear of retaliation. Whistle-blowers can be current or former employees, or business associates, and they can report concerns either anonymously or with their identity disclosed, using secure channels.
The goal is to create a transparent, ethical environment that ensures lawful practices, protects public health and safety, and promotes the company's commitment to integrity.
## SCOPE
This policy applies to all employees, ex-employees, and business associates of the company.
## POLICY
- Encourage employees, ex-employees, and business associates to report suspected unethical behavior, financial fraud, violations of company policies, or wrongful conduct, including breaches of law or public safety.
- Foster a culture of transparency, trust, and accountability within the organization.
- Ensure confidentiality and protection for whistle-blowers, with timely action on reported concerns.
- All reports should be made in good faith, with supporting evidence.
## QUALITATIVE OBJECTIVES:
- Encourage transparency, honesty, and accountability throughout the organization.
- Strengthen the company's ethical culture by empowering employees and business associates to speak up without fear of retaliation.
- Ensure that complaints are handled with the highest degree of confidentiality and integrity.
- Foster an environment where unethical behavior is addressed swiftly and effectively.
## QUANTITATIVE OBJECTIVES:
- Review and act on any whistle-blower complaints within 30 days of receipt.
- Ensure 100% confidentiality of all whistle-blowing complaints, including those made anonymously.
## PROCEDURE
## MAKING A DISCLOSURE
- Employees, ex-employees, or business associates can make a disclosure by phone or in writing to the Audit Committee Members, providing supporting evidence where possible.
- The disclosure should be based on good faith belief that the information evidences one of the following concerns:
- Violation of law or regulation (e.g., corruption, theft, fraud, bribery, coercion).
- Financial malpractices such as procurement frauds, misappropriation of funds, or manipulation of company records.
- Misuse of company assets or human resources, including theft or unauthorized use of company materials.
- Any discriminatory behavior or violations of the company’s Code of Ethics and Conduct.
- Abuse of authority or harassment (including sexual harassment).
- A substantial threat to public health and safety.
## DISCLOSURE INVESTIGATION
- The Audit Committee will investigate any disclosure within 30 days of receipt.
- Based on the investigation’s findings, the Audit Committee may:
- Close the complaint if the conduct is unsubstantiated.
- Recommend corrective actions if the complaint is substantiated.
- Suggest improvements to company policies or procedures to prevent future occurrences.
- Management will take appropriate action based on the Audit Committee’s recommendations.

chapters.title: Promotion Policy
chapters.text:
## Objective
This policy aims to develop existing employees to meet the organization's future needs and provide them with career advancement opportunities. Promotion is a systematic and periodic process designed to assess individual job performance, productivity, and contribution to organizational objectives. Performance appraisals are conducted to evaluate employees’ abilities, competencies, and overall value to the organization.
## Scope
This policy applies to all permanent employees of Efficient Plastech Private Limited.
## Policy Statement
Efficient Plastech Private Limited is committed to promoting employees based on merit, performance, and organizational needs while ensuring non-discrimination and equal opportunity throughout the promotion and development processes. The organization upholds the principles of fairness, equity, and inclusion, explicitly prohibiting discrimination on the basis of gender, age, religion, caste, disability, marital status, sexual orientation, or any other personal attribute. The promotion process is structured to be transparent, data-driven, and free from favoritism or bias.
## Qualitative Objectives
- Employee Development: To foster the growth of employees by providing advancement opportunities based on skill and merit.
- Fairness and Equity: To maintain a transparent and unbiased promotion system that rewards performance and aligns with organizational goals.
- Organizational Growth: To identify and nurture talent that contributes to the organization’s
strategic priorities and long-term success.
- Performance Enhancement: To encourage employees to set measurable goals and achieve continuous improvement in their performance.
- Non-Discriminatory Advancement: Ensure equal opportunity and inclusion in professional growth without discrimination or bias.
## Quantitative Objectives
- Promotion Rate: Ensure that at least 80% of promotions are tied to measurable performance metrics and evaluation scores.
- Employee Participation: Achieve 100% participation in annual performance evaluations by all eligible employees.
- Skill Matrix Updates: Conduct skill matrix evaluations twice a year for all employees.
## Governance and Responsibility Mechanism
## HR Department:
- Distribute and collect performance appraisal forms.
- Coordinate the promotion process, ensuring consistency across all departments.
- Monitor adherence to policy guidelines and detect potential bias or favoritism.
- Ensure promotion decisions comply with inclusion and non-discrimination principles.
- Maintain records for audit and transparency.
## Managers/Supervisors:
- Conduct goal-setting and performance planning meetings.
- Provide continuous and constructive feedback.
- Evaluate employee performance based on pre-defined metrics and values.
- Recommend employees for promotion based on documented merit.
- Provide upskilling support to bridge performance or skill gaps.
## Employees:
- Actively participate in planning, feedback, and evaluation discussions.
- Align personal development goals with organizational objectives.
- Seek and participate in training programs for skill enhancement.
## Top Management:
- Approve final promotion decisions based on documented evaluations.
- Ensure organizational fairness in promotion trends across functions, genders, and levels.
- Periodically review promotion data to identify and correct disparities.
- Address grievances or disputes related to promotion or professional development.
## Performance Cycle:
- The performance cycle runs from 1st April to 31st March.
- Performance evaluations must be completed, approved, and discussed with employees by 15th March.
## Performance Management Process: The process is divided into three stages:
## Performance Planning:
- Each employee sets at least four strategically aligned goals.
- Managers discuss and finalize performance plans with employees.
## Performance Feedback:
- Ongoing feedback and two formal reviews (mid-year and end-of-cycle) are conducted.
- Managers document observations and provide actionable feedback to employees.

chapters.title: Annual Performance Evaluation:

- Assessment is based on achievements, behavior, and company values.
- Evaluation is evidence-based and includes scoring against agreed KPIs.
## Skill Matrix:
- Conducted biannually to assess individual and team competencies.

## Promotion and Increment:
- Determined based on cumulative evaluation scores.

## Accessibility and Inclusion in Professional Development
- Employees with disabilities are provided with reasonable accommodations in training and evaluation processes.

Promotions must not be influenced by:
- Subjective opinions unsupported by documented evidence.
- Favouritism, nepotism, or any personal relationships.
- Direct or indirect discrimination based on gender, age, caste, religion, disability, or any other characteristic.
- Fraternization or influence from external or unrelated parties.
- Retaliation, bias, or omission of due process.

chapters.title: Health And Safety Policy

Efficient Plastech Private Limited is committed to developing and promoting a healthy and safe working environment for all employees and visitors. Through education, communication, and safe work practices, the organization fosters a culture of safety and well-being. - Foster a safety-first culture where employees prioritize health and safety in their daily activities.
- Promote employee awareness and education on safety practices and hazard prevention.

This policy defines the procedures and eligibility criteria for employees who are preparing for retirement. It is important to note that EFFICIENT PLASTECH PRIVATE LIMITED does not have a mandatory retirement age. This policy applies to all full-time and part-time employees.

In accordance with applicable laws and regulations, employees are not required to retire. However, employees become eligible to retire at the end of the month in which they turn 58 years.

potential successors within 6 months prior to an employee’s retirement.
- Maintain continuity of operations by having clearly documented standard operating procedures (SOPs) and work manuals for roles that are retiring.
## Quantitative Objective:
- Ensure that 95% of retiring employees complete the knowledge transfer and transition activities within the 12-month notice period.
## GOVERNANCE AND RESPONSIBILITY ALLOCATION

## Responsibilities:

chapters.title: Child Labour, Forced Labour, and Human Trafficking
chapters.text:
The Company is committed to upholding human rights and ensuring that its operations, as well as those of its suppliers and business partners, are free from child labour, forced labour, and human trafficking. We believe in fair treatment, dignity, and respect for all individuals involved in the supply chain and business activities.
The Company strictly prohibits the use of child labour in any part of its operations, directly or indirectly. As a minimum, employees must meet the legal working age of year 18 years requirements as outlined by local laws and international standards.
- What to Do: Ensure that all workers are above the legal working age and provide a safe, supportive working environment for all employees, particularly those in youth or apprenticeship programs.
- What Not to Do: Do not engage in any form of employment that involves individuals below the legal working age or expose them to hazardous work conditions.
The Company does not condone the use of forced, bonded, or involuntary labour in any of its operations. All employees are to work voluntarily, without coercion, and with the ability to leave employment freely.
- What to Do: Ensure that all employment agreements are voluntary, transparent, and comply with local and international labour laws. Provide employees with the freedom to choose their employment without any form of force or threat.
- What Not to Do: Do not employ any individuals under conditions of forced, bonded, or involuntary labour, including withholding passports or identity documents, or engaging in practices that restrict freedom of movement.

## Human Trafficking
The Company condemns human trafficking in any form, including the recruitment, transportation, or harboring of individuals through force, fraud, or coercion for exploitation.
- What to Do: Adopt procedures to ensure that no employees or workers are victims of human trafficking. Provide proper training to employees and management to recognize and report signs of human trafficking.
- What Not to Do: Do not engage with any individuals or businesses involved in human trafficking activities. Do not tolerate or ignore any signs of trafficking within your workplace or supply chain.
## Monitoring and Reporting
Employees, contractors, and suppliers are encouraged to report any incidents or suspicions of child labour, forced labour, or human trafficking to the designated authority within the company (e.g., HR, Compliance). The Company will take immediate action to investigate any reported concerns and will cooperate with relevant authorities to address such issues.
## What to Do
- Ensure that all employees meet the legal working age and are employed voluntarily.
- Adopt fair employment practices and ensure no individual is subjected to forced or involuntary labour.
- Report any suspected cases of child labour, forced labour, or human trafficking to the appropriate authority immediately.
- Provide training on human rights issues to employees and suppliers.
## What Not to Do
- Do not employ individuals below the legal working age or expose them to hazardous working conditions.
- Do not engage in or tolerate forced, bonded, or involuntary labour practices.
- Do not ignore or cover up any suspected instances of human trafficking or related activities.

## OVERVIEW
This policy aims to ensure consistent administration of attendance management and establish the responsibilities of employees and supervisors regarding attendance.
## SCOPE
This policy applies to all Permanent and Contractual Employees.
## POLICY
Good attendance is essential to the smooth functioning of the company. Employees are expected to make every reasonable effort to be present as scheduled, arrive on time, take breaks punctually, and provide timely notice of situations affecting attendance. Supervisors are responsible for monitoring attendance, engaging with employees on attendance issues, and ensuring appropriate corrective actions are taken.
## Qualitative Objectives
- Employee Engagement & Accountability: Foster a culture where employees feel responsible for their attendance and the impact of their presence on team performance.
- Open Communication: Encourage employees to report potential attendance issues early and provide support where necessary, fostering an atmosphere of trust.
- Well-being Support: Address absenteeism resulting from health concerns in a compassionate manner, ensuring that employees are supported while also maintaining operational efficiency.
## Quantitative Objectives
- Attendance Rate: Achieve an attendance rate of 85% or higher across all departments, ensuring minimal disruptions to workflow.
## CORRECTIVE ACTION CATEGORIES
- Acceptable Absenteeism: When an employee is absent due to serious illness for extended or repeated periods, this will be assessed on a case-by-case basis. ## PURPOSE
To provide clarity and guidance on decisions relating to the receipt of gifts and hospitality by Efficient Plastech Private Limited staff and expenditure on the same for the staff or others. The intention is to ensure staff exercise integrity and financial prudence so that risks associated with sensitive transactions are minimized.
## SCOPE
This policy applies to all employees of Efficient Plastech Private Limited and any third party acting on behalf of Efficient Plastech Private Limited.
## POLICY PRINCIPLES
Sensitive transactions are those of a discretionary nature where there is or is perceived to be, personal benefits in addition to the benefit to Efficient Plastech Private Limited. They often arise in the context of hospitality, travel, or appreciation of professional service.
- Ethical Responsibility: Employees must exercise judgment and discretion when engaging in sensitive transactions. All expenditures must align with the company's objectives and values, ensuring the company's integrity is maintained.
- Transparency & Accountability: Employees must declare gifts, hospitality, and travel exceeding Rs. 5,000 to the management. All sensitive transactions should be documented and authorized in accordance with company guidelines.
- Moderation & Documentation: Sensitive expenditures should always be moderate, related to the objectives of Efficient Plastech Private Limited, and appropriately authorized and documented.
## QUALITATIVE OBJECTIVES
- Promote Ethical Behavior: Encourage employees to act with integrity, avoiding actions that could create conflicts of interest or damage the company's reputation.
